messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Seg fault from temporaries?
parts:
Does this model seg fault for anyone else in develop?

parameters {
real mu[50];
}

model {
real temp;
print("temp = ", temp);

mu ~ normal(0, 1);
}

The set fault seems to occur as soon as the temp, defined as a real in the model block, is accessed.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Seg fault from temporaries?
parts:
Yes, there is an issue for this I think. Locals in the model block are not initialized to NaN or anything else, so you can get segfaults.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Seg fault from temporaries?
parts:
On Jun 25, 2013, at 6:21 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:

> Does this model seg fault for anyone else in develop?
>
> parameters {
> real mu[50];
> }
>
> model {
> real temp;
> print("temp = ", temp);
>
> mu ~ normal(0, 1);
> }
>
> The set fault seems to occur as soon as the temp, defined as a real in the model block, is accessed.

Yes, it seg faults on me. Is this issue #91? https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/91

I think I know what's going on. When temp is declared, it is called with the default constructor. This sets the vi_ pointer in the var to 0. operator<< for var is where it's dying. If we replace operator<< with something like (in src/stan/agrad/rev/var.hpp):
friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const var& v) {
if (v.vi_ == 0)
return os << "uninitialized";
return os << v.val() << ':' << v.adj();
}

we should be ok. Bob, is that message good for an uninitialized value? The output for the model will then look like:
temp = uninitialized

Is it too slow to have an if there? Is the preference to initialize it to NaN?



Daniel
Í

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Seg fault from temporaries?
parts:
On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 8:37:16 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
Is it too slow to have an if there? Is the preference to initialize it to NaN?

I think it would be preferable to initialize it to NaN. That is what we do with other things and also would prevent the segfault no matter what the model does with uninitialized variables.

Ben
